subject: Clarifying per-call floor for mixed short/long context workloads
messages:
From: Lina Torres <lina@novamed.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions about per-call floor and long-history calls

Hi Markus / Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — Novamed's product team liked the latency profile. Before procurement signs the SOW we have one technical/pricing clarification that will affect commit math for our three-month pilot.

Our workload is mixed: many short validation calls (~30-120 tokens) and periodic long review sessions (full patient history ~8k-12k tokens). Procurement wants to understand exactly how the per-call minimum (the "floor") and rounding rules will apply across these patterns, and how KV/prefix reuse reduces chargeable units. Specifically: 

- If a short call follows a long review and reuses a cached KV prefix, is the short call still charged at the full per-call minimum?
- Does streaming generation (server-side streaming) change how we are rounded to the minimum?
- Are there any credits for repeated prefix reuse within a billing window (24h)?

Attached is our sample usage for last month so you can model it (novamed_sample_usage.csv).

Can you provide a short example invoice line and a one-paragraph explanation we can put into the internal procurement memo?

Appreciate it — Lina

Lina Torres
Director, ML Platform
Novamed
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Torres <lina@novamed.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions about per-call floor and long-history calls

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear examples and the CSV. Looping in Kimberly (pricing lead) and Sergio (partner success) to make sure we capture any commercial concessions.

Short answers up front, and then a short invoice example below. Full modeled walk-through attached (Novamed_SOW_v1.pdf).

1) Per-call minimum: each request is evaluated for chargeable units after accounting for KV/prefix reuse. If the server determines a KV hit (prefix fully satisfied from cache for the same conversation id within the window), token usage attributable to response generation can be reduced. However, the per-call minimum still applies to the aggregated metered units for that request — so a short call that ends up with < minimum billable units will be rounded up. Put plainly: cache reuse lowers billed tokens but does not eliminate the call-level minimum unless you have commit credits that offset it.

2) Streaming: charges are computed on the final realized token count for the call. If you stream the same sequence but stop early, we bill for tokens produced. Rounding to the minimum is applied after streaming finalization, so truncated streaming still sees the per-call floor.

3) Prefix reuse credits: we offer a limited intra-window re-use credit policy — for high-frequency identical prefixes we apply a small prefix-reuse multiplier that effectively reduces billed tokens for subsequent identical hits within a 24h window. This is not a guarantee in the SOW unless explicitly contracted; for pilots we can include a nominal reuse credit for identical prefix hashes (see attached concession language).

Example invoice line (single daily summary):
- Date: 2028-04-12 | Model: rwd-gpt-xl | Calls: 12,345 | Raw tokens billed: 8,742,300 | Prefix reuse credit: -12,300 tokens | Applied per-call minimums: +18,000 tokens | Net billable tokens: 8,748,000 | Unit price: $0.0008/token | Line total: $6,998.40

Notes: the "Applied per-call minimums" line is the cumulative uplift after rounding each call to the minimum. In this example many short calls drove the +18k uplift.

Next steps: Kimberly, can you confirm whether we want to include a pilot-level prefix reuse credit in the SOW and the size (suggest 0.25% of billed tokens for identical hashes in-window)? Sergio, can you own an internal runbook for how support will tag these calls if Novamed asks for retroactive adjustments?

— Markus

Markus Klein
Sr. Dir, Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference
From: Lina Torres <lina@novamed.com>

Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions about per-call floor for mixed short/long context workloads

Thanks Markus — that's very helpful. Two quick clarifications from procurement: 

- Can the per-call minimum be applied at the session level for our long-review flows (i.e., amortize short subsequent probes within a session to the session minimum) instead of per HTTP call? That would materially reduce the uplift for our use-case.
- For the prefix reuse credit, procurement would like clear language: when exactly do you consider two prefixes "identical" (hash of conversation + model + last-token-offset)?

If you like, we can do a 20-minute call to walk the CSV and make sure the example invoice aligns with how we'll ingest telemetry. Are you able to do Wednesday morning?

Lina
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Torres <lina@novamed.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions about per-call floor for mixed short/long context workloads

Hi Lina — quick reply after reviewing Markus's example and our legal team's SOW templates. Short answers and a proposed concession.

1) Session-level amortization: we can include a pilot concession that allows calls sharing a session_id within a 2-hour session window to amortize the per-call minimum across that session. Mechanic: we calculate total billable tokens for the session and apply a single session minimum equal to max(session_calls * per-call-minimum, session_minimum_floor), then distribute billing at the call level for telemetry. This is a pilot concession (three months) and would be explicitly listed in the SOW.

2) Prefix identity: for the reuse credit we define "identical" as an exact match on the prefix-hash computed from (model_name, conversation_id, prefix_token_count, prefix_sha256). We'll add that definition into the SOW and include a clause that allows audit sampling for disputes.

3) Size of credit: for the pilot we propose a 0.3% gross token credit applied against the monthly invoice line for eligible prefix hits, capped at $5,000 for the pilot term. This is intended to be a goodwill concession and not a long-term contract term.

Next steps: if that sounds acceptable, we will: (a) update the SOW with the session amortization language and prefix-hash definition, (b) attach a one-paragraph explanation for procurement to include in your memo, and (c) schedule a 20-minute call for Thursday 10:00–10:30 PT to review the CSV.

Please confirm and we'll send the redlined SOW (I attached a draft: redlines_novamed_sow.docx) and the memo paragraph.

Thanks — Kimberly

Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Pricing & Commercials
